disguised_difficulty: L5 is essentially the core transformed positivity statement. This is acceptable because it is explicitly presented as the bottleneck, but it carries most of the proof burden and is close to the parent theorem on the natural subfamily d>=m arising in the assembly.
fixes_required: Step A0 claims triviality but requires multiple introduction/discharge operations (introducing arbitrary n, k, l in range and the temporary assumption H). Break into smaller steps or surface the intermediate reasoning as a lemma.

assembly_plan.proof_skeleton_nl: Fix arbitrary n, k, l in the allowed range and assume the quotient is polynomial. Replace k and l by k0 = min(k, n-k) and l0 = min(l, n-l) using q-binomial symmetry, and use the degree obstruction to force l0 <= k0. Rewrite the reduced quotient as a shifted interval ratio F_{b,m,d}(q) with b = l0, m = k0 - l0, and d = n - k0 - l0. The cyclotomic exponent formula converts polynomiality of F_{b,m,d}(q) into the floor-count condition saying that every modulus t sees at least as many multiples in the shifted numerator interval as in the denominator interval. The bottleneck positivity lemma for shifted interval ratios then shows that F_{b,m,d}(q), hence the original quotient, has nonnegative coefficients. Finally discharge the temporary polynomiality hypothesis and generalize over n, k, l.

steps.derives: Fix arbitrary integers n, k, and l with 0 <= k <= n and 0 <= l <= n, and assume H: the rational function [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q is a polynomial in q.
steps.trivial_justification: This is the standard setup for proving the universally quantified implication in the theorem.

steps.derives: Let k0 := min(k, n-k) and l0 := min(l, n-l). Then [n choose k]_q = [n choose k0]_q and [n choose l]_q = [n choose l0]_q, so [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q = [n choose k0]_q / [n choose l0]_q. In particular, H implies that the reduced quotient [n choose k0]_q / [n choose l0]_q is also a polynomial in q.
steps.trivial_justification: Because k0 is either k or n-k, L1 gives [n choose k]_q = [n choose k0]_q; similarly, because l0 is either l or n-l, L1 gives [n choose l]_q = [n choose l0]_q. Substituting these two equalities into the quotient gives equality of the original and reduced rational functions. Since H says the original quotient is polynomial, the reduced quotient is polynomial as well.

steps.derives: The reduced indices satisfy k0 >= l0.
steps.trivial_justification: L2 applies directly to the same integers n, k, and l under the hypothesis H and yields min(k, n-k) >= min(l, n-l), which is exactly k0 >= l0.

steps.derives: From the definitions of k0 and l0, we have 0 <= k0 <= n/2 and 0 <= l0 <= n/2; together with A2 this gives 0 <= l0 <= k0 <= n/2. Define b := l0, m := k0 - l0, and d := n - k0 - l0. Then b, m, and d are nonnegative integers.
steps.trivial_justification: By definition of minimum, both k0 and l0 are at most n/2 and are nonnegative. A2 gives l0 <= k0, so m = k0 - l0 >= 0. Also d = n - k0 - l0 >= 0 because k0 <= n/2 and l0 <= n/2 imply k0 + l0 <= n. Hence b, m, d are all valid inputs for the shifted interval product.

steps.derives: The reduced quotient can be rewritten as [n choose k0]_q / [n choose l0]_q = F_{b,m,d}(q) = product_{i=1}^m (1 - q^(b+d+i)) / (1 - q^(b+i)).
steps.trivial_justification: A3 gives exactly the hypotheses 0 <= l0 <= k0 <= n/2 needed for L3. Applying L3 with l = l0 and k = k0 rewrites the reduced quotient in the stated shifted interval form; because b = l0, m = k0 - l0, and d = n - k0 - l0, this rewritten product is exactly F_{b,m,d}(q).

steps.derives: For every positive integer t, floor((b+m)/t) - floor(b/t) <= floor((b+d+m)/t) - floor((b+d)/t).
steps.trivial_justification: By A1 the reduced quotient [n choose k0]_q / [n choose l0]_q is a polynomial. By A4 this reduced quotient is exactly F_{b,m,d}(q). Lemma L4 says that F_{b,m,d}(q) is polynomial if and only if the displayed floor inequalities hold for every positive integer t. Therefore those inequalities are valid for the present b, m, and d.

steps.derives: The polynomial F_{b,m,d}(q) has only nonnegative coefficients.
steps.trivial_justification: A5 verifies exactly the hypothesis of L5 for the integers b, m, and d chosen in A3. Therefore L5 yields that F_{b,m,d}(q) lies in Z[q] and every coefficient in its q-expansion is nonnegative.

steps.derives: The reduced quotient [n choose k0]_q / [n choose l0]_q has only nonnegative coefficients.
steps.trivial_justification: A4 identifies the reduced quotient with F_{b,m,d}(q), and A6 proves coefficientwise nonnegativity for that polynomial. Substituting the equality from A4 transfers the coefficientwise nonnegativity to [n choose k0]_q / [n choose l0]_q.

steps.derives: Under the temporary hypothesis H, the original quotient [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q has only nonnegative coefficients.
steps.trivial_justification: A1 shows that the original quotient equals the reduced quotient, while A7 shows that the reduced quotient has only nonnegative coefficients. Therefore the original quotient has only nonnegative coefficients as well.

steps.derives: For all integers n, k, and l with 0 <= k <= n and 0 <= l <= n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.
steps.trivial_justification: The argument started with an arbitrary triple n, k, l satisfying the bounds and an arbitrary assumption H that the quotient is polynomial. Step A8 derived the desired coefficientwise nonnegativity from H. Discharging H proves the implication for this arbitrary triple, and universal generalization yields exactly the theorem statement.

lemmas.statement_nl: For integers b, m, and d with b >= 0, m >= 0, and d >= 0, define F_{b,m,d}(q) := product_{i=1}^m (1 - q^(b+d+i)) / (1 - q^(b+i)), with the empty product equal to 1 when m = 0. For each positive integer t, the exponent of the cyclotomic polynomial Phi_t(q) in the factorization of the rational function F_{b,m,d}(q) is (floor((b+d+m)/t) - floor((b+d)/t)) - (floor((b+m)/t) - floor(b/t)). Consequently, F_{b,m,d}(q) is a polynomial in q if and only if floor((b+m)/t) - floor(b/t) <= floor((b+d+m)/t) - floor((b+d)/t) for every positive integer t; in that case F_{b,m,d}(q) actually lies in Z[q].
lemmas.strictly_easier_reason: This is a cyclotomic factor-counting statement about divisibility, independent of any coefficientwise positivity.
